Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The umpires are back out in the middle and the players of Bangladesh can be seen in a huddle. It will be the pairing of Pathum Nissanka and Kusal Mendis to open the innings for Sri Lanka. Mohammad Saifuddin to take the new ball for Bangladesh. Let's go...
... The Run Chase ...

Sri Lankan pacers used this slow wicket well, as they kept on hitting the deck and varying their pace, which made the batter’s task difficult. In the spin department, Jeffrey Vandersay bowled a superb economical spell of 4-0-25-1, operating in the middle overs. Theekshana too was tidy except for his expensive over in the powerplay, as he finished with 2 wickets for 37 runs. Now the wicket is on the slower side, and Bangladesh does have 12 overs of spin to make full use of the slowness of this wicket. Sri Lanka pacers bowled a lot of slower ones, which were hard to hit. Bangladesh must have surely picked it up. So, the job is not going to be straightforward for the home side. Do join us for the chase in some time.

That will be the end of the Bangladesh innings. They finish with 154 on the board, which seems below par. To start the proceedings, the visitors had a strong 46-run first-wicket partnership as Emon dominated the PP phase. However, he perished immediately post powerplay, losing his wicket to Theekshana for a quickfire 38. As spinners took over, post-powerplay runs dried down, and the next 7 overs produced just 39 runs for 3 wickets, as batters found it hard to attack on this slow wicket. However, a crucial 46-run partnership between Mehidy and Naim and a handy little knock towards the end from Shamim Hossain, saw the visitors cross the 150-run mark as they finished with a total of 154.

Just a single to end proceedings here! Goes full and wide, Mohammad Naim leans on and crunches it away towards deep cover. The batters try and push for the second run but the fielder in the deep is quick to get to the ball. 11 off the final over and Bangladesh finish with 154/5 on the board!

Commentary.Commentary: Done and dusted with the pre-match formalities and it is now time to get the match underway. The umpires are out in the middle and so are the Sri Lankan players, who form a huddle before taking their places on the field. It will be the duo of Parvez Hossain Emon and Tanzid Hasan to open the innings for Bangladesh. Chamika Karunaratne has the new ball in hand and raraing to go. Let's play...

Right then, time for the national anthems as it is the first game of the T20 series. The players lineup along with the mascots and it will be the national anthem of Bangladesh first, followed by that of Sri Lanka.

PITCH REPORT - Farveez Maharoof, the former Sri Lankan all-rounder is inspecting the deck. Reckons that this pitch looks pretty similar to the one from a couple of days back but seems drier. Adds that it was surprising to see Sri Lanka field first and they will look to keep Bangladesh under 170-180 runs. Ends by saying that overall, the conditions look good and the outfield is lightning fast.

Litton Das, the captain of Bangladesh, says that the wicket looks pretty good to bat on and will look to get a good score on board. Reckons that they have good balance in the side with 6 batters and 5 bowlers. Adds that most of the team played in the ODIs and are confident and a few guys have come in for the T20s and are looking forward to it.

Charith Asalanka, the Sri Lankan captain, says they will bowl first. He adds that in T20s his team is happy to chase on these kind of grounds. He mentions that they are going with 6-5 combination with a couple of all-rounders as well. He tells that they are still searching for their best combination looking forward to the 2026 T20 World Cup.

Bangladesh (Playing XI) - Litton Das (C/WK), Tanzid Hasan, Parvez Hossain Emon, Mohammad Naim, Tawhid Hridoy, Mehidy Hasan Miraz, Shamim Hossain, Mohammad Saifuddin, Taskin Ahmed, Rishad Hossain, Tanzim Hasan Sakib.

Sri Lanka (Playing XI) - Pathum Nissanka, Kusal Mendis (WK), Kusal Perera, Avishka Fernando, Charith Asalanka (C), Dasun Shanaka, Chamika Karunaratne, Maheesh Theekshana, Jeffrey Vandersay, Binura Fernando, Nuwan Thushara.
TOSS - Sri Lanka win the coin flip and have elected to BOWL first.

With just about 5 or so minutes left to toss, the big blow for Sri Lanka will be the absence of Wanindu Hasaranga, who pulled his hamstring in the final ODI and has been ruled out of the T20I series. Wanindu can't catch a break in terms of injuries. Also, it is a public holiday in Sri Lanka and a few sources are saying that the tickets for this game have been sold out.

The pitch at Pallekele is expected to offer a balanced surface, with early swing and seam for pacers before becoming more conducive for batting as the game progresses. Sri Lanka holds an overall T20I head-to-head advantage, winning 11 of the 17 matches played. However, it's worth noting that Bangladesh has a surprisingly strong record at Pallekele, maintaining an unblemished 3-0 record against Sri Lanka at this venue. This historical quirk adds an intriguing dimension to what promises to be a gripping opening encounter. Stay tuned for the toss and team news.

On the other hand, Bangladesh will be eager for a fresh start in the T20I format under new captain Litton Das, aiming to put their recent setbacks in the longer formats behind them. While their recent T20I form has been challenging, including a 3-0 whitewash against Pakistan and a surprising loss to UAE, they historically have a decent T20I record against Sri Lanka, winning 6 out of 17 encounters. The Tigers will need their key players like Mustafizur Rahman and Tawhid Hridoy to fire if they are to challenge the hosts.

Hello, and a warm welcome to one and all. The highly anticipated three-match T20I series between Sri Lanka and Bangladesh kicks off with the first T20I at the Pallekele International Cricket Stadium. Sri Lanka enters this shortest format with significant momentum, having already clinched the Test series 1-0 and the ODI series 2-1 on home soil. They will be keen to maintain their dominance and complete a clean sweep across all formats, leveraging their strong home advantage and a settled squad.
... MATCH DAY ...

Tests? Ticked off. ODIs? Accounted for. Now, with two formats in the rear-view, the spotlight shifts, but stays white-hot, as Sri Lanka and Bangladesh dive into the fast lane of cricket’s most explosive format: the T20Is. Home turf has been Sri Lanka's stronghold, and their recent form only reinforces that dominance. The ODI victory by 2-1 has added to an unbeaten streak that now stretches to eight consecutive series since 2021. In T20Is, they’ve continued to hold their ground, winning four out of their last six home series. The only setbacks were a drawn series against New Zealand and a clean sweep handed by India in 2024. Aside from those blips, Sri Lanka have ruled the roost. Sri Lanka's 17-player squad balances promising youth with seasoned heads, steered by the astute Charith Asalanka. The left-handed batter, thriving at No. 4, will aim to anchor the middle order with calm efficiency. Wanindu Hasaranga, fresh off a sensational ODI series, remains the side’s trump card in all departments. Maheesh Theekshana, with his deceptive carrom ball and wrong’un, is expected to thrive on the turning home tracks. Veteran presence is abundant in Kusal Perera, Dasun Shanaka, and Dinesh Chandimal, each bringing tactical depth and match awareness across different roles. While the core resembles the ODI squad, some notable additions inject fresh energy. Chamika Karunaratne, returning to T20Is for the first time since 2023, strengthens the lower order and seam attack. Joining him is debutant Eshan Malinga, whose slingy action and raw pace have earned him a long-awaited cap, promising a new dimension to Sri Lanka’s bowling arsenal. He will join the elite forces in the form of Matheesha Pathirana, Nuwan Thushara, and Binura Fernando's pace triumvirate. With a good balance between the bat and the ball, this Sri Lankan squad is set towards bagging another series at home. 2025 has been a turbulent year for Bangladesh in T20Is, marked by frustration and missed opportunities. Back-to-back away series defeats, first a clean sweep at the hands of Pakistan, followed by a shocking loss to the UAE, have left the Tigers scrambling for form and answers. Their only shining moment remains the convincing 3-0 triumph over the West Indies earlier in the year, a performance they’ll be desperate to recreate. In a bid to reset their fortunes, Bangladesh turn to Litton Das, the dependable wicketkeeper-batter, to take over the captaincy reins. The squad’s core remains largely intact, mirroring Sri Lanka’s approach. Mehidy Hasan and Tawhid Hridoy will be crucial cogs in the batting setup, both capable of anchoring and accelerating when needed. The pace attack is loaded with firepower. Mustafizur Rahman's crafty death bowling, Taskin Ahmed, and Tanzim Hasan Sakib's raw pace, and Shoriful Islam's left-arm angle give the team versatility in all phases. But it’s the spin department that could dictate Bangladesh’s success on Sri Lankan soil. The turning tracks will demand precision from Nasum Ahmed and the promising Rishad Hossain, while Mehidy Hasan Miraz is expected to play a dual role, bolstering both the spin attack and the lower-order batting. With conditions stacked against them, Bangladesh’s blend of experience and youthful exuberance must fire collectively if they’re to break the drought and reclaim their rhythm in T20Is. Now this is where the plot thickens. Pallekele, the venue for the opening T20I, hasn’t exactly been a happy hunting ground for Sri Lanka in recent years. Of their last 10 outings here, they’ve emerged victorious just twice, their most recent win dating back to 2022 against Australia. Strengthening their patchy Pallekele resume will be a priority, especially with the rest of their home venues offering a far more favorable record. Adding intrigue to the storyline is Bangladesh’s spotless history at this venue. The last time these two sides met at Pallekele was in 2013, and Bangladesh have maintained an unblemished 3–0 record here. It’s a statistic that not only boosts their morale but also gives Sri Lanka a clear challenge. Lastly, in the last five head-to-head clashes, it’s been an even contest with Sri Lanka just edging their rivals by 3-2, with their last meeting in Dallas, in the T20 World Cup 2024. We sure talk about the major rivalries in cricketing landscapes, but when it comes to the subcontinental thrillers, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh have definitely produced some absolute close games. Expect this series to be no different.
